bounded_statement: The selected result reports a two-sample Student t-test with t(38) = 10.89, p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 3.44 computed on all 40 chamber-visit rows (n = 20 per management class), even though the declared independent unit is plot_id and there are only 10 plots (5 per class), each contributing 4 repeated readings from the same patch of peat. Each independent unit therefore enters the row-independent t-test four times, inflating the effective sample size and degrees of freedom (38 instead of 8 at plot level), so the reported test statistic, p-value, and effect size are not supported at the declared unit of independence. This finding is bounded to the inferential quantities: the direction of the difference (restored > drained) is consistent with plot-level means and is not itself contested.

counterevidence_considered.description: A reader could argue that each row is a distinct static-chamber deployment ('on every visit one static chamber was deployed'), suggesting physically separate measurement events; however, the same description states that readings sharing a plot identifier come from the same patch of peat and names plot_id as the independent unit, so this does not establish row-level independence.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: one fresh chamber deployment per plot per visit

counterevidence_considered.description: Severity mitigation rather than refutation: the plot-level means computable from the data (restored plots ~8, 10, 12, 14, 16; drained plots ~2, 3, 4, 5, 6) are cleanly separated, so a correctly specified plot-level comparison (n = 5 per group) would very likely still find a significant restored > drained difference; the direction of the stated conclusion is robust even though the reported t(38), p-value, and Cohen's d are anti-conservative.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the verdict three ways. (1) I checked whether the workflow aggregates or otherwise accounts for plot before testing: flux_by_group() iterates over raw rows and appends one flux value per row, and the string 'plot_id' never appears in workflow/analysis.py, so no aggregation, blocking, or mixed-effects structure exists. (2) I checked whether the group counts could plausibly reflect independent units: the report shows 20 'measurements' per group, but the description and CSV show only 5 plots per group, so 20 can only arise as 5 plots x 4 visits, confirming repeated entry of each unit. (3) I checked whether the rows could be independent despite sharing plot_id: the description explicitly names plot_id as the independent unit and says rows sharing a plot identifier come from the same patch of peat, and the data show strong within-plot clustering (e.g., PEAT-R1: 7.4, 7.8, 8.2, 8.6), so treating rows as independent is not defensible. All three falsification routes failed, so the demonstrated-issue verdict stands; the only surviving caveat is that a correct plot-level analysis would likely preserve the direction of the effect, which does not negate that the reported inferential statistics are computed on pseudoreplicated rows.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py never uses the plot_id column: flux_by_group() appends every CSV row's ch4_flux_mg_m2_h value to a per-management list, and stats.ttest_ind() is applied directly to these row-level lists (20 values per group). No aggregation to one value per plot (or any repeated-measures/mixed-model structure) is performed, so each of the 10 independent plots is entered four times into a procedure whose validity assumes each entry is an independent observation.
